history: Fotocopia joins two old words from two languages. Foto- is the Greek stem for light, phōs, phōtós, the same as in fotografia, ‘drawing with light’. Copia is Latin, and at first it meant ‘plenty, abundance’, as in the English word cornucopia. In Medieval Latin copia came to be used for a written copy: to make many versions of a text was to give it abundance. Italian copia has that meaning today, as in fare una copia. The compound fotocopia is a modern word of the twentieth century, first for copying by a photographic process, later for any copier. At the Comune and the Questura you will often hear ‘una fotocopia del documento’: bring a copy of your passport or permesso di soggiorno.
